categories.name: Photo editing
categories.summary: Ordinary raster work is broad and locally exercised; the active release pass is tightening real-photo colour, precision and scale evidence.

items.name: Core raster editing
items.current: Brush, Pencil, Eraser, Fill, Gradient, Crop, Resize, Move, Clone, Blur, Smudge, Liquify, Heal, Spot Heal and destructive filters are wired into the native editor with undo/redo. Moving rotated/reflected layers preserves their transforms; proportional resizing can cross its anchor, and corner distortion preserves pixel orientation without baking stationary clicks.
items.boundary: Bounded local journeys do not establish every brush size, transform, colour space or long-session workload.

items.name: Selections and selection-aware edits
items.current: Marquee, ellipse, lasso, wand, object selection, feathered coverage and selection-aware filters/content fill are implemented; the hardened paths preserve soft coverage and undo.
items.boundary: Quality still depends on the source and tool settings; physical input delivery is a separate desktop gate.

items.name: Retouching and controlled removal
items.current: Local Spot Healing, Clone/Healing, content-aware fill, healing layers, frequency separation and controlled removal are implemented. Final 189f3e7 Cua check removed a synthetic blemish with J, then with Ctrl+K Content-aware fill; each restored it with one Ctrl+Z. Engine tests cover exact selection/undo integrity and allowed sampling areas.
items.boundary: The manual explains local versus AI removal and limits. Controlled removal has a 4 MP input ceiling; ordinary fill is bounded to 16,777,216 source pixels and 250,000 selected pixels. Synthetic checks do not establish complex photographic reconstruction quality. Later 0.9 astronaut Spot Heal testing duplicated nearby lettering/zipper detail: numeric corpus success is not a clean-retouch claim. Choose clean donors and inspect the result; use Clone or reviewed AI reconstruction where local texture is unsuitable. New versioned controlled removal is tracked separately.

items.name: Versioned controlled removal with boundary context
items.current: The final 0.9 runtime uses ContextualV1 boundary-guided controlled removal; its photo library source is unchanged from tested 8f72ce5c. Thirty focused tests passed, including ten new regressions. The portrait check preserved all 256,052 protected pixels, single-step Undo/Redo, atomic cancellation, retained source/16-bit samples and saved recipe re-evaluation. The final archive reopened/exported the cache exactly through 0.8 → 0.9 → rollback → forward.
items.boundary: Sources are limited to 4,000,000 pixels and additional work limits. Some seam/texture mismatch remains: preview, choose clean nearby donors, refine selection/feather and use Clone/AI when needed. Numeric correctness is not universal quality. Omuse 0.8 can display the cache but editing/resaving can discard ContextualV1; keep the 0.9 original and rasterize a separate copy before backward editing.

items.name: Adjustments, filters and editable stacks
items.current: Exposure, levels, curves, hue/saturation, colour balance, blur, sharpen, denoise, grain/noise, vignette, bloom, tonal contrast, invert and grayscale are available through destructive and editable paths.
items.boundary: The Camera Raw compatibility node remains an 8-bit path; not every traditional adjustment/effect can be exported at full precision.

items.name: Camera Raw scopes and preview responsiveness
items.current: RGB histogram and hue/saturation vectorscope use bounded alpha-weighted samples. Camera Raw adds stage-aware neutral white-balance and defringe sampling, targeted curve/HSL drags, and one active plus one newest queued preview. Cancelled and stale work cannot replace another document or dialog.
items.boundary: Six numerical gesture cases, four GUI gesture cases and lifecycle checks pass within the release suite. Full-resolution 8-bit grading is limited to 16 MP; canvas references are bounded. Scopes/samplers describe display RGB, not sensor RAW/HDR; no comparative speed claim.

items.name: Embedded RAW development
items.current: LibRaw import retains original bytes and a 16-bit editable source. After visual review rejected a grossly magenta result, the corrected Nikon and Canon outputs both match the independent C++ camera-white-balance PPM16 references exactly for every retained sample and were visually inspected as natural.
items.boundary: The earlier two-camera evidence uses the same pinned LibRaw engine, not an independent audit of LibRaw colour science or a general camera-colour claim. The earlier 734-test suite passed with the Nikon RAW fixture enabled; the full 16-case corpus was not repeated for the history/ownership or photo-integrity changes.

items.name: Real-photo and large-document qualification
items.current: The 16 photo cases passed at ac8874d. The isolated region-history workload at a69a5f6 passed 18 runs with 100 strokes, exact final undo/redo pixels, .omuse save/reopen and PNG export; routine medians were 2.00/2.13/0.42 ms at 12/24/48 MP. The later desktop ownership comparison is recorded separately below.
items.boundary: The earlier isolated editor fixture measured median peak RSS of 326/610/1200 MiB and does not establish physical input latency. The later desktop fixture also waits for recovery before painting. Rapid strokes during background work, native large-camera decode and long sessions still need qualification.

items.name: Region/tile-based large-photo history
items.current: Large unselected Brush, Pencil and Eraser strokes retain reversible 256×256 tiles. Current differential regressions pass. Historical a69a5f6 measurements retained 100 undo steps at 48 MP using about 30.96 MiB of final history, compared with one step before.
items.boundary: Masks, selected strokes, clone/heal and other transactions keep snapshots. Persistent Create raster owners are now removed, but recovery, collection checkpoints and saves can still force copies. The earlier 12/24 MP first strokes were slower; neither workload qualifies whole-app input latency.

items.name: Large-photo desktop page ownership
items.current: Editors own active and cached page pixels; complete save/export/recovery snapshots remain frozen. All 18 paired cases passed. At 48 MP, paint core measured 85.69 → 0.32 ms and headless frame/refresh 257.88 → 165.38 ms. Editing during a same-path save can recover, export and save again.
items.boundary: Twelve localized strokes after a warmup, three repetitions per strategy/size; recovery idle before each measured stroke. Peak RSS was essentially unchanged. In-flight snapshots can still force full copies, and end-of-stroke refresh has large outliers. These are not physical input timings.

items.name: Interactive crop and photo/social ratios
items.current: Crop opens a movable frame seeded from the selection or full canvas. Free, Original, 1:1, 4:5, 3:2 and 16:9 presets, orientation swap, corner resizing, arrow nudging and Apply/Cancel are implemented. Original pixels remain in their layers; Apply is one undo step.
items.boundary: Automated/native/Cua checks passed on 0.3.0. Integer output can round a ratio by one pixel; crop rotation and perspective correction are separate tools.

items.name: Responsive outlines for complex selections
items.current: Zoom-aware background outlines, visible-region clipping, cancellation and a 65,536-point display cap. Exact selection pixels remain unchanged.
items.boundary: Contour, selection-generation and combined UI regressions passed. One immutable selection snapshot is copied per generation. Exact masks remain unchanged; no comparative speed measurement.

items.name: Dither, halftone and retro image effects
items.current: Ten deterministic Dither styles plus Bloom Glow, Vignette Overlay and Local Contrast. The finishing panel previews, applies cached exact pixels and supports selection-aware Undo.
items.boundary: Engine, Apply/Undo, selection and lower-controls scrolling/typing regressions passed. Production Dither/Bloom/Vignette panels were inspected in dark/light themes. Requires 8-bit raster copies and canvases/layers up to 16 MP; retained masters stay unchanged.

items.name: Smudge, Liquify and brush-region blur
items.current: Released 0.8.0 samples Liquify from the original stroke source, carries a continuous fading Smudge trail, and limits Blur work to the affected area plus its sampling halo. Focused kernel/transaction tests and isolated CPU comparisons accompany the implementation.
items.boundary: Isolated 8MP kernel measurements are not end-to-end pointer latency. Broad photographic retouch quality and large transformed-layer work remain separate qualification. The 0.9.0 native-resolution rewrite is tracked separately and must not inherit the earlier timings or qualification.

items.name: Camera Raw curve semantics and graph refinement
items.current: Compare smoother parametric bends and an RGB master curve against the existing luminance-first recipe. Point dragging already preserves its captured point and order; region/divider gestures and a selected-point readout are proposed refinements.
items.boundary: Changing curve or Refine Saturation meaning needs explicit recipe/version compatibility so existing saved grades keep their appearance. Add independent reference pixels and gesture regressions first; this is not Photoshop colour certification or a shipped 0.6.0 change.

items.name: Scanlines and CRT finishing
items.current: A distinct Scanlines/CRT finish is a candidate addition identified in the new upstream roadmap. Current Omuse Dither exposes ten existing styles, including halftone lines and ASCII.
items.boundary: Halftone lines are not a separate CRT mode. No new effect was implemented or qualified in this review; preview/Apply, selection, transparency, cancellation and Undo would need coverage.

items.name: Complete photo precision and export fidelity
items.current: Approved P01/P02: the development branch passed bounded sampling, alpha/mask and cancellation checks for the new 16-bit renderer. Removing the Camera Raw 8-bit bottleneck and extending full-precision effects remain planned.
items.boundary: Installed/public 0.7.0 is unchanged. Reduced masked detail can still differ between the 8-bit canvas and 16-bit export. Complete high-precision editing and independent photographic quality remain unqualified.

items.name: Measured camera and lens profiles
items.current: Approved P03: camera/lens identification, compatible calibrated profiles, manual overrides and independently reviewed colour-chart/correction cases.
items.boundary: Current generic correction controls are not a measured camera/lens profile database. Camera support, profile licensing and real-input quality remain work.

items.name: Reference-photo colour matching
items.current: An editable Match reference colour filter borrows a reference palette with amount and preserve-lightness controls, native file selection, preview, masks and Undo. Native 16-bit sRGB, linear and Display P3 sources retain their precision.
items.boundary: Global statistics transfer, not semantic object or lighting correspondence. Stores bounded statistics, not the reference image/path. References are bounded to 16MP and 128MiB. Campaign-wide consistency needs broader photographic review.

items.name: Detail-preserving restoration and enlargement
items.current: Approved P08: learned denoise, deblur, enlargement and optional scratch/face/text recovery, with detail comparison and retained originals.
items.boundary: Current local restoration uses conventional filtering/resizing. Model availability, licence, Linux execution, generated-detail behaviour and resource cost require evidence before integration.

items.name: Depth masks and editable relighting
items.current: Approved P09/P12: editable depth masks, separate near/far brightness and warmth, portrait/product relighting and edge/halo correction.
items.boundary: No current depth-based relighting implementation. Depth estimates and difficult hair/transparency need correction controls and independent image review.

items.name: Robust, re-editable multi-image merges
items.current: Approved P10: rotation/perspective registration, panorama projection, focus-blend improvements, HDR moving-subject handling and retained merge recipes.
items.boundary: Current merges are translation-only, bounded to 16 MP output and normalize HDR into 16-bit linear sRGB; no persistent 32-bit radiance or editable merge history.

items.name: Target colour uniformity — 0.7.0
items.current: Omuse 0.7.0 runtime 5b3daefbb5258afff4a74a2ff3db5247b074972d provides an editable Filter stack node with a reference colour, circular hue range/falloff and independent hue/saturation/lightness strengths. Native 16-bit evaluation, alpha, node opacity and selection masks are retained.

A project containing this new node requires the 0.7.0 reader; retain a 0.6-compatible copy with Save As. See docs/release-070-qualification.md.

items.name: Inspect the actual JPEG before export
items.current: Fit/100% physical-pixel views and drag/arrow panning inspect the actual encoded JPEG. Compact quality, resolution and matte RGB controls include a live swatch.
items.boundary: JPEG preview supports its existing pixel/work limits and does not change the saved document. Compact JPEG behavior passes GPUI; the b47 full-size native screenshot is retained, while a new compact-window resize capture was unavailable.

items.name: Preserve the endpoint at the retouch capture limit
items.current: The 0.9.0 candidate uses one bounded pointer-path capture for deferred raster and selection gestures. Consecutive duplicate positions, including mouse-up, do not consume a point; a genuinely over-limit or invalid path is cancelled explicitly before artwork changes instead of silently losing its tail.
items.boundary: Limit: 100,000 recorded points. Duplicate release, retained corners/reversals and unchanged pixels/history on overflow passed in the final Linux/Windows suites. Physical long-drag and trackpad stress remain separate from these bounded checks.

items.name: Retouch at native layer resolution
items.current: The 0.9.0 candidate applies Blur, Smudge and Liquify directly to native layer or mask pixels, including scaled, rotated, anisotropic and flipped placement. Soft selections constrain final writes while neighbouring source colours remain sampleable. Blur has a separate 0.25–128 canvas-pixel Radius control; source alpha, pixel dimensions, mask extent and stored outside coverage are retained.
items.boundary: Requires an 8-bit raster layer or existing mask up to 16 MP, with a 256 MiB working-buffer budget and bounded work. Shear/excessive footprints are refused; released strokes have no interactive Escape cancellation. The unchanged photo library passed 16 cases / 128 operations on working copies at most 1,024 pixels wide, including transformed soft selections and mask Liquify. Final Linux/Windows regressions passed; this does not qualify every large-photo workload or physical input device.

items.name: Cancellable background retouch
items.current: Omuse 0.10: Blur, Smudge and Liquify calculate raster and mask strokes on a background worker. Escape or Cancel · Esc discards pending work; successful results publish as one Undo step. Captured editor/page, selection and target identity reject stale results.
items.boundary: Historical development Linux suite: 1,422 passed, four ignored, including ten retouch UI cases; final native XWayland Smudge/Undo/Redo smoke passed. Editing/Create/motion journeys and all 80 template variants passed. One image worker per editor window remains admitted until completion, including after cancellation. Existing 16 MP / 256 MiB bounds remain; selection capture and final canvas refresh still run on the UI thread. Final Linux/Windows automated CI passed; no new speed, interactive Windows or photographic quality claim.

Final Linux/Windows automated CI passed; interactive Windows, native Wayland and GPU processing remain unqualified.

categories.name: Layers and masks
categories.summary: The native document model covers hierarchy, editable effects and multiple mask types with bounded persistence and transaction tests.

items.name: Layer hierarchy and compositing
items.current: Pixel layers, groups, transforms, opacity, blend modes, clipping, visibility, locking, reorder/copy and grouped editing are implemented. Clipped groups retain independent live-mask links on descendant layers in both renderers.
items.boundary: Cross-window layer drops and complete parity with every legacy Mac gesture remain outside the current evidence.

items.name: Raster, linked and folder masks
items.current: Per-layer masks, detached placement, link/unlink behavior, live alpha links and folder masks persist through project save/reopen.
items.boundary: Mask growth is implemented in the separate 0.6.0 growing-masks card. Rasterization and document limits remain bounded; older project versions cannot represent every newer mask feature.

items.name: Adjustment layers and layer effects
items.current: Hue/Saturation, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Gradient Map and Grain adjustment records coexist with stroke, shadows, colour overlay and outer glow effects.
items.boundary: Legacy-reader support varies by project version, and 16-bit export rejects unsupported traditional adjustment/effect records rather than flattening silently.

items.name: Editable filter stacks and Blend If
items.current: Retained sources support ordered filter nodes, opacity, selection masks and backdrop-aware Blend If with channel controls.
items.boundary: Editable layers are capped at 128 nodes; source and mask storage budgets apply, and evaluation remains CPU-heavy for large images.

items.name: Hue, colour and luminosity range masks
items.current: The 0.8 candidate adds circular hue selection across changing brightness, saturation protection for greys and softness, alongside RGB distance and luminosity ranges. Replace/Add/Subtract/Intersect and layer-mask outputs preserve soft coverage.
items.boundary: Mask pixels are persisted, not a reopenable range recipe. Existing refinement correction strokes still bake their results.

items.name: Vector masks
items.current: Cubic path geometry remains editable while its vector mask is rasterized into layer coverage; path Apply rebuilds that coverage transactionally.
items.boundary: This is a bounded path/mask workflow, not compound-path boolean authoring or a complete vector illustration system.

items.name: Editable layer clipboard and Linux image exchange
items.current: Copy without a pixel selection retains complete selected trees, masks, transforms, locks and advanced sources in the running Omuse session. Paste remaps internal identities and commits once. Native Wayland and XWayland PNG exchange preserved exact source pixels. Bounded nonblocking writes keep the UI responsive to slow readers; delayed pastes reject stale state and active interactions. Unsafe or no-op pixel/mask cuts preserve the previous clipboard.
items.boundary: Payload is capped at 256 MiB and the full-resolution PNG at a 16 MP source canvas. Missing mask dependencies reject. Separate processes, clipboard managers and app restarts do not carry editable trees. An idle reader can retain its transfer buffer until it closes.

items.name: Paint masks beyond their original bounds
items.current: Brush, fill and gradient masks can grow while preserving placement, linked/detached geometry, outside coverage and original layer pixels.
items.boundary: New and existing mask regressions passed in the combined suite. Expansion has a 16 MP interactive cap with failure rollback. Outside coverage and grown folder-mask placement require canvas format 10.

items.name: Persistent range, refinement and semantic masks
items.current: Approved P04: retain mask recipes/correction strokes; select person, hair, clothing and face regions, then add/subtract/intersect and refine manually.
items.boundary: Existing selection/refinement results do not establish complete semantic masking or retained correction histories. Qualify varied real subjects and preserve source pixels.

items.name: Mask inspection and safe folder ungroup

The windows CI job runs the test suite and the editing, Create, template catalog and motion journeys, then keeps the unsigned zip as a 14-day workflow artifact. omuse.exe carries the Omuse icon and version information, follows the Windows light or dark app mode, starts save dialogs in the Pictures or Videos known folder (including OneDrive redirection) and accepts long paths; package moves retry for up to 10 seconds while a sync client or scanner holds a file. Ask Omuse finds codex.exe or claude.exe on PATH, recognises npm's Codex launcher and runs its native binary, gives job, sign-in and probe workspaces an access list for the current user only, hard-links Codex credentials into its isolated home and passes Windows' essential environment to providers.

Windows has no atomic directory exchange: replacing a project moves the previous package to a hidden sibling between two renames.
